name: get_context
description: Where you are: the local frame and direction rules, the size tier and allowed box, the dimension, biome, time and weather, the ground block at the origin, where the player stands (local) and how many tool calls are left. Call it first.

name: survey_area
description: The terrain around the site as compact text: floor heights (y relative to the ground at the origin), surface blocks, water and lava, trees, cave ceilings and protected (probably player-made) regions as local boxes. Default radius covers the allowed box with 8 blocks to spare; at most 96. Read it before designing.

name: inspect_region
description: The exact blocks in a local box [x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2] (at most 4,096 blocks), layer by layer with a palette, directions relative. Use it to check what is already there, or to check your own work.

name: search_blocks
description: Find block ids by words ("oak stairs", "copper lantern"), other mods' blocks included, each with its properties and allowed values (directions as relative words).

name: submit_brief
description: Describe the build before placing any block: a title, a style, the size you're aiming for, a palette of 4-8 blocks with roles (primary, secondary, accent, trim, roof, glass, floor, light) and the phases you'll build in. The player sees a one-line summary. Required before every other write tool.

title.description: What you're building, a few words.

style.description: The style, e.g. gothic, rustic, japanese.

size.description: Planned width (x), height (y) and depth (z) in blocks.

phases.description: The phases in order, e.g. foundation, walls, roof.

name: set_blocks
description: Place individual blocks, up to 2,000 per call. Positions are local: +x is the player's right, +z forward (away from the player), +y up, y=0 the ground at the origin. Block states use forward, back, left, right, up, down for directions, never compass names. Prefer the shape tools for anything regular.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

block.description: Block id, e.g. oak_door or minecraft:stone_bricks; other mods' ids work too.

name: fill
description: Fill a box [x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2] (local, inclusive, corners in any order). mode: solid (default) fills it; hollow makes the shell and clears the inside to air; outline makes the shell and leaves the inside alone; replace places only where the current block matches filter (a block id or #tag).

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

filter.description: For mode replace: the block id or #tag to replace.

name: line
description: A straight line of blocks from one local position to another, both ends included.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

name: wall
description: A vertical wall along a polyline of [x, z] points, height blocks tall starting at y. Close a loop by repeating the first point. Extra thickness grows to the right of the walking direction.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

name: cylinder
description: A cylinder: discs of the given radius stacked height blocks along axis (y by default, or x or z for one lying on its side), starting at center. hollow keeps only the outer ring. Good for towers and pillars.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

name: sphere
description: A ball around center; hollow keeps only the shell; dome keeps the upper half (y at or above the centre).

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

name: cone
description: A cone from a disc at base_center narrowing to a point height blocks up; hollow keeps each layer's ring. Good for spires and tower caps.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

name: arch
description: An arch between two feet at the same y, in a straight line along x or z, rise blocks high at the middle. style: round (default) or pointed (gothic). Extra thickness grows to the right of the from-to direction.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

name: roof
description: A roof built correctly from stairs and slabs, starting at the box's lowest y over its footprint grown by overhang (0-2) on every side. style gable: two slopes up to a ridge along ridge (x or z; default the longer side), an odd width needs slab for the ridge row, gable_block fills the two triangular end faces. hip: slopes on all four sides. flat: one layer of slab.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

stairs.description: A stairs block id, e.g. spruce_stairs.

slab.description: A slab block id, e.g. spruce_slab.

name: staircase
description: Stairs you can walk up. style straight: steps going direction (forward, back, left, right) from from, one up per step, width wide to the right of direction. style spiral: one step per level from from_y to to_y round the ring radius blocks from center's column (leave the column for a pillar), clockwise by default.

part.description: Optional: make these blocks a moving part with this name (lowercase, like left_wing): displays that look exactly like the blocks but can move, with no collision, and that animate gives their motion. Keep the solid body as ordinary blocks (leave part out). The same name adds to the same part. Doors, beds and tall plants can't move.

name: clear
description: Set a box [x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2] to air. Blocks that look player-made stay unless include_protected is true; blocks that can't be broken (bedrock) always stay.

part.description: Optional: take a moving part's blocks in the box out (its displays there go) and leave the world's blocks as they are. Without it, clear leaves moving parts alone.

include_protected.description: Also remove blocks that look player-made. Only when the player asked for it.

name: terraform
description: Level the box's footprint (its y range is ignored) to target_y, which must be inside the allowed box's height, from the ground as it is now (what you queued earlier is placed first): everything above target_y becomes air up to each column's highest block (trees too), the ground below is filled up with fill_block (default dirt, replacing any water or lava), and target_y gets surface_block. Protected blocks stay. Use it to make a flat site, a terrace or a raised plinth before building.

name: place_block_entity
description: Dress the build: a sign with text, a chest, barrel, shulker box, dispenser, dropper or decorated pot with items, a lectern with a written book, a banner with patterns, or an item frame holding an item. Give pos and exactly one of sign, container, lectern, banner or item_frame. For the first four also give block (and state, as for set_blocks): a sign block (oak_sign, oak_wall_sign, oak_hanging_sign…), a container, lectern, or a banner (white_banner, red_wall_banner…; the block's color is the base). A sign takes up to 4 lines a side (about 15 characters show on a line), a dye color and glowing; a container up to 27 stacks, filled from the first slot (nothing that holds items itself); a book up to 50 pages of 800 characters, though a page shows only about 250 (line breaks kept); a banner up to 6 patterns, each a pattern id and a dye color, bottom layer first. An item frame is an entity, not a block: give no block; pos is the empty spot in front of a solid block, facing the way the frame looks out (forward, back, left, right, up, down). Text is stored as plain text.

pos.description: [x, y, z] in the local frame

state.description: Property names to values, directions relative

color.description: A dye color: black (default), white, red, blue, …

pattern.description: stripe_bottom, border, cross, creeper, flower, skull, globe, bricks, gradient, rhombus, circle, half_horizontal, …

facing.description: forward, back, left, right, up or down: out of the block it hangs on

name: checkpoint
description: Wait until everything queued so far is placed, then report progress; the player's status shows the phase. Call it at the end of each phase.

name: check_build
description: Wait until everything queued is placed, then look the build over in the world: unsupported blocks (a torch on air, sand over a drop), dark walkable spots under a roof (monsters spawn at block light 0), doors that can't be walked through, rooms lower than 2 blocks, and water or lava that would flow if disturbed (an open side, or air under a pool's edge). Positions are local, at most 60 listed, grouped by kind. Call it before finish, fix what matters, and call it again.

name: animate
description: Give a moving part its motion, replacing any it had; build the part first (part on a write tool). pivot: the point it turns about, in block units where a whole number is a block's centre and .5 the face between two (a wing's hinge at its shoulder, [0.5, 8, 4]); within 16 blocks of the allowed box. motions, 1 to 8, applied in order: {"swing": {"axis", "from", "to", "period", "phase"?}} turns back and forth between two angles in degrees (-180 to 180), from at the start and to half a period later; {"spin": {"axis", "period", "phase"?}} turns a full turn each period (a negative period turns the other way); {"bob": {"direction", "distance", "period", "phase"?}} moves back and forth up to distance blocks (at most 16). Axes and directions are forward, back, left, right, up or down. A positive angle turns clockwise as you look along the axis: about forward, the part's top moves to the right; about up, a part in front of the pivot moves to the left. period: ticks for one cycle (20 ticks a second), 10 to 2,400; phase: 0 to 1, to put parts out of step (a tail a little behind the wings). parent: another part this one rides with (at most 4 deep, never itself). A spin about a pivot outside the part carries it round in a circle. Examples: a right wing hinged on the body's top right edge, {"swing": {"axis": "forward", "from": 30, "to": -40, "period": 40}} (down at the start, up half-way; the left wing from -30 to 40); windmill sails as one part, {"spin": {"axis": "forward", "period": 160}} about the hub; a dragon circling a tower, its body a part spinning about up with the pivot at the tower's centre and its wings parts with parent body. Then call check_motion.

name: check_motion
description: Look over the moving parts after animating them, as check_build looks over the blocks: for each part, the box it fills as built and at the start, a quarter, half and three quarters of its longest cycle (so you see where a wing goes as it flaps), and the solid blocks, the build's or the world's, it passes through over a cycle (a wing through the body, a blade through the ground), the lowest few listed. Fix what's wrong (the pivot, smaller angles, the part a block further out) and look again. It waits for what's queued first.

name: test_redstone
description: Try the build's machine in the world, over game ticks (20 a second): steps run in order. {"set": [x, y, z], "on": true} flips a lever the build placed on or off; {"press": [x, y, z]} presses a button it placed; {"wait": ticks} lets the machine run; {"read": [[x, y, z], …]} says what's at each spot and its state (a lamp lit, a dust's power, a repeater powered, a piston extended, a door open, a torch lit). At most 64 steps, 400 ticks of waiting in all and 32 spots a read, all inside the allowed box. It waits for what's queued, then gives the build's redstone its shape and starts it as if placed by hand (each piece once), and afterwards puts every lever it flipped back as it was. It refuses while check_build would list a piston, powers_outside or feeds_dispenser problem, and won't press a button within 2 blocks of something that reacts to power and isn't the build's. While a player stands where one of the build's pistons would push, the next change waits for them (at most 30 seconds), then the test stops. One test at a time. A machine isn't done until it's been tested for every case that matters: each input combination of a small one, the edge cases of a big one.

name: place_gadget
description: Place a ready-made, tested redstone part (a gadget) and join its ports with wire. Kinds and options: lever_row {bits 1-8 (default 4), label (a short lowercase word, default in)}: levers on posts, a sign on each saying the row and what the bit is worth, an output behind each; lamp_row {bits}: an input before each lamp; adder {bits 1-8}: adds a and b, inputs a0…, b0… and the carry in c0 on its front, the sum s0…s<bits> out its back. at: the gadget's front-left-bottom block; facing: the way its outputs run (forward, right, back or left; default forward); its inputs are on the opposite side, its front. It's placed whole or not at all: its box must be inside the allowed box, hold nothing player-made, and keep a block from every other gadget; it clears its box first. The answer gives its box, each port's spot (a wire's end dust goes there), the spots to test (its levers, its lamps) and how many ticks it takes to settle after an input changes; wait at least that long in test_redstone.

name: finish
description: End the build. The summary is shown to the player.
